newsitem.title: UK: BA says American link will raise competition.
newsitem.headline: BA says American link will raise competition.

text.p: British Airways told the European Commission on Tuesday that it believed its proposed alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines on trans-Atlantic routes would increase competition, not diminish it.

In a statement on the UK airline's 148-page response to the Commission, BA said the alliance was a competitive response to alliances already in place, citing those between United Airlines of the U.S. and Germany's Lufthansa and Scandanavia's SAS, between Delta of the U.S. and Belgium's Sabena and Swissair.
"It will provide customers with more competition and more choice and means better services and keener fares," said BA in a statement.

The response follows comments by the European Commission's competition commissioner Karel van Miert on Monday that the EC would not tolerate British approval of the deal if it conflicted with EC views.
But BA said it remained confident of its deal with American remaining on track. It said that the EC had not reviewed other similar alliances even though some were larger than the BA/American deal.
British Airways added that other continental airlines had an even "larger share of the markets between their home countries and the U.S."
The UK airline said the EC did not take into account that UK clearance of the merger hinged on an open-skies agreement being clinched between the UK and U.S. governments on transatlantic routes.

This would lead to a scrapping of the existing restrictions if it goes through. The next set of open-skies talks are due in early February in the U.S.. Such a deal would benefit other U.S. airlines as well, said BA.
BA estimates that an open skies deal could increase the size of the total UK/U.S. market by 20 percent, feeding new competition.

It concluded that it and American understood that "under article 89 of the (European) Treaty of Rome, the UK Department of Trade and Industry working with the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) has the power in Europe to rule on the alliance."
